session_1758597966875_zehrd0g: To what extent do you support or oppose upzoning policies that allow for higher density housing in traditionally single-family neighborhoods? Please explain your reasoning.
column3: I'm a big fan of this proposal. I just see major advantages to it with very little downside. It improves the community, helps the local economy flourish and creates new opportunities for the disadvantaged.

session_1758597966875_zehrd0g: What do you think are the most significant impacts, positive or negative, of increasing housing density in residential neighborhoods?
column3: The first thing that comes to mind is that it will make housing more affordable. This means that low-income individuals will have an easier time finding a place to live. Because, cost-effectively, it is cheaper to build vertical, this will result in lower housing prices. Everyone benefits there. As I mentioned before, it will also bolster the economy, because more people will be available for businesses.

session_1758597966875_zehrd0g: How do you think upzoning policies might affect housing affordability in urban areas?
column3: It should make them more affordable as there are more homes on the market. This makes it less scarce because there are more buildings for buyers to choose from. By building vertically, you increase the density which will result in more real estate efficiencfy.

session_1758597966875_zehrd0g: What impact do you believe increased housing density might have on neighborhood character and quality of life?
column3: I imagine it will only improve it. More people will increase the diversity and make the neighborhood more vibrant. It will also open up more opportunities for businesses. New restaurants could be built for example. The city will look more modern.

session_1758597966875_zehrd0g: How do you think upzoning might affect transportation systems and traffic congestion in cities?
column3: Should improve it as there will be less need for cars. Public transportation like railways work well in big cities and the density will make the area very walkable. Lots of places are located nearby, and not far away.

session_1758597966875_zehrd0g: What role do you believe local government should play in regulating housing development and density?
column3: I believe the city council could play a role in this. They could establish guidelines based on zoning and other factors. They could also consider input from local residents, businesses and their constituents.

session_1758597966875_zehrd0g: How might environmental concerns factor into decisions about urban density and zoning?
column3: They would likely have to undergo environmental studies before starting on major construction. Pay attention to the local habitat as we want to protect the animals and their ecosystem. It's also important to consider renewable energy sources such as solar or wind

session_1758597966875_zehrd0g: What economic effects, both positive and negative, might result from changing zoning laws to allow more multi-family housing?
column3: First, the negative effects. It will be an investment, so the city should lose money in the short term while they build the developments. It could take years before a return on investment. On the plus side, it should bolster the local economy as more affordable housing means people will have more money to buy things, which should keep local businesses afloat.

session_1758597966875_zehrd0g: How do you think the interests of current residents versus future residents should be balanced when making zoning decisions?
column3: Like I said earlier, it is important to give local residents a voice in the manner. The city council should take into consideration their thoughts. But at the same time, progress must be made towards the future generations.

session_1758597966875_zehrd0g: What role do you think social equity and access to opportunity play in discussions about zoning and housing policy?
column3: Not everyone has the same advantages. Some people, due to socioeconomic factors struggle to get ahead and have a hard time affording basic housing. To be fair to these groups, we need to give them a chance, to the disadvantaged, so to speak.

session_1758597966875_zehrd0g: Is the effect of Higher density housing on Support for Upzoning immediate, or does it take time to develop? Does it have a positive effect (increasing it) or a negative effect (decreasing it)? How strong is this effect?
column3: Like I said, it is an investment, so it will take time to see a return. In the short term the city loses money because of the high costs. It will take a while for people to move in and get acclimated for example. Over time, it should be a positive for the community.

session_1758597966875_zehrd0g: What factors do you think influence Support for Upzoning, and how strong is their impact? Please also indicate if these influences are positive (increasing) or negative (decreasing).
column3: Business come to mind because upzoning leads to more customers which will mean more revenue for them. I imagine it would be a strong positive impact. Also, it would be fairer to those with less money, as they do not have the same opportunities as the wealthy. So to speak, it would level the playing field.

session_1758597966875_zehrd0g: Is the effect of Housing affordability on Support for Upzoning immediate, or does it take time to develop? Does it have a positive effect (increasing it) or a negative effect (decreasing it)? How strong is this effect?
column3: Housing affordability should be a quick help as people will be able to quickly find homes. Currently, they may be out of their budget and may just be waiting for prices to drop. They should immediately jump on the opportunities, so effects should be seen fairly quickly. It has a strong positive effect because the community should prosper more.

session_1758597966875_zehrd0g: Is the effect of Lower housing prices on Support for Upzoning immediate, or does it take time to develop? Does it have a positive effect (increasing it) or a negative effect (decreasing it)? How strong is this effect?
column3: Could take time to develop. Developers are making a big investment and will start off at a loss. They spend tons of money on these projects and would like to see the fruits of their labor pay off. They will want as many units open as possible as this will increase their rent. With a lot of units, the money should start to add up.

session_1758597966875_zehrd0g: How would you describe the relationship between Neighborhood character and Support for Upzoning? Is it a strong or weak connection? Does it have a positive effect (increasing it) or a negative effect (decreasing it)? How strong is this effect?

It's a strong connection as it makes the areas more lively and vibrant. This means more parks, restaurants, businesses, buildings, etc. so it is a strong positive effect.

session_1758597966875_zehrd0g: How would you describe the relationship between Diversity and Support for Upzoning? Is it a strong or weak connection? Does it have a positive effect (increasing it) or a negative effect (decreasing it)? How strong is this effect?

But by opening more doors, you allow new residents to come in, hailing from different backgrounds. This will make the area more diverse as the demographics open up.

This means more opportunities. The strength of the effect, which should be a positive, will depend on how substantial the shift is.

So it might not be as bad as you would think.
